questions.question: What is the approximate ideal ratio of iron ore, coking coal, and limestone required to produce steel in an integrated blast furnace?
questions.explanation: Iron ore, coking coal, and limestone are required in roughly the ratio of 4 : 2 : 1. Some quantity of manganese is also required to harden the steel.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes Mini Steel Plants from Integrated Steel Plants?
options: Mini steel plants handle everything from raw iron ore melting to steel shaping in one complex
Mini steel plants use electric furnaces, sponge iron, and steel scrap, producing mild and alloy steel of specified sizes
Integrated steel plants operate exclusively in rural villages without electricity
Mini steel plants can only manufacture agricultural ploughs
questions.explanation: Mini steel plants are smaller, have electric furnaces, use steel scrap and sponge iron. questions.question: What is the function of limestone in the blast furnace during the smelting of iron ore?
options: It provides the thermal combustion fuel to melt iron
It hardens steel into stainless alloy
It removes moisture from coking coal
It acts as a flux that combines with impurities to form slag
questions.explanation: Limestone is added to the blast furnace as a fluxing material. It reacts with silica and alumina impurities in the iron ore to form molten slag, which floats on top and is separated from molten iron.
